authors: T. Enns, P. F. Scholander, E. D. Bradstreet
title: Effect of Hydrostatic Pressure on Gases Dissolved in Water
experimental_method: Water saturated with gas near atmospheric pressure is held in a pressure chamber at 0-102 atm hydrostatic pressure; the gas equilibrium pressure is found by a null-point measurement of pressure developed inside a gas-permeable Teflon tube immersed in the solution.
uncertainties_stated: None given for the table values.
quality_remarks: Water vapour pressure was subtracted from all gas pressures. Partial molal volumes are average values from straight lines through ln p versus hydrostatic pressure; the authors say all gases except He actually give slightly curved plots. The table holds no dissolved-gas concentrations, so it is not a solubility table; only the derived partial molal volume (and the raw equilibrium pressures) are given. PDF page 1 begins with Table VIII of another article (heats of formation of XO3 species) which is not this paper's. Header row 'P = 102' for the He first row carries footnote b (102.7 atm). Temperature scale not stated.
not_extracted_tables: Table VIII on journal p. 389 (heats of formation of ClO3, BrO3, IO3): belongs to a different article, out of scope
row_counts: Table 1: printed 16 data rows, written 16 data rows plus 8 label rows (24 rows after header)
changes_after_image_check: none (text layer garbled only in gas label cells: 'O' read as CO2, '8156' read as 815 with footnote b, first-row 'o2'/'n2' case; corrected from image before writing)
extraction_notes: Printed decimal forms such as '.133' kept as printed. 'O2 at 0.5 C' printed as 0.5 degrees. Table is a mix of gas rows in distilled water, one sea-water row and one detergent row. Text layer was partly garbled so the table was written from the image.
